chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever carries a weapon at night is a muharib, unless he is a man not suspected of wrongdoing."

key_terms.الرِّيبَةِ: suspicion or grounds for distrust in conduct
key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: weapon or arms carried by a person
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: during the night, indicating a legally relevant circumstance
key_terms.رَجُلًا: a man, referring here to the person carrying the weapon
key_terms.مُحَارِبٌ: one deemed to be engaged in hostile armed wrongdoing

ai.seo_question: When is carrying a weapon at night considered an act of muharabah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion related to armed conduct at night and its presumptive classification as hostile or criminal behavior. It also notes an exception for a person who is not regarded as suspicious, indicating that circumstances and known character affect legal judgment.
